decisionsTitle: The backoffice's status chip: the public glyph table keeps only public names
decisionsSection:
**Why.** §694 made `GlyphChip` the one chip and left about a dozen names in the public glyph table (`modules/events/ui/glyphs.ts`) that only the backoffice draws, so every visitor's bundle carried backoffice icons. The owner's standing rule is fast and clean; the header and the landing page are what every visitor pays for (`AGENTS.md` §1.5).

**Decision.** The backoffice has its own chip, `StatusChip` (`src/shared/ui/StatusChip.tsx`), with its own registry `src/shared/ui/status-glyphs.ts`, one file per glyph (§90). The look is `GlyphChip`'s: small, the palette's colour tokens, the glyph before the words; it has no tooltip, link or screen-reader extras. The twelve names that moved, none drawn by any public file: `done`, `cancelled`, `open`, `planned`, `building` (a state's or a plan's step), `visible`, `hidden`, `language` (a row shown or hidden, a one-language text), `shop`, `orders`, `club`, `link`. Their call sites are the team page and its boxes, the shop's product page, product list and orders card, the members' zone's order chip (a signed-in surface, not a public one) and the design page. The public table keeps what public pages draw: types, surfaces, difficulty, cost, the card's marks, `person` for the team card's fold. `GlyphSelect` and the staff preview draw public names and stay on `GlyphChip`'s table.

**A server chip or an island?** The server chip was tried first, in thought: MUI's `Chip` is a client component, so an `icon={<Icon />}` made in a Server Component reaches it as a lazy Flight reference, `isValidElement` says no and hydration fails (§370, the defect `GlyphChip` records). `GlyphButton` and `panel-glyphs` can draw a glyph server-side only because the glyph is a child, not a prop of a client MUI component. A chip that keeps MUI's `Chip` look cannot, so `StatusChip` is a second small client island that takes a name and makes the element on its own side; the cost is one island whose table holds twelve icons rather than the public one's forty.

**The tripwire.** `tests/unit/design/status-chip.test.ts`: the two tables share no name; no public file imports `StatusChip`; every status name is drawn by a file that imports it; every plain public name is drawn by a public file. `status-glyphs.ts` is an icon registry and `StatusChip.tsx` a primitive file in `guards-allowlist.ts`; the ratchet's numbers do not move (no allowlisted file was fixed). `/admin/design` → «Iconografie» shows the new table with its count.

**Refused.** One registry for both chips (it is the thing that sent backoffice icons to visitors); a second icon family; moving `GlyphChip`'s tooltip and link features into the new chip (nothing in the backoffice uses them).
changelogLine: - **Visitors download fewer icons** — the backoffice's status chips have their own small registry (`StatusChip`), so twelve backoffice-only glyphs leave the public chip's table; nothing changes on screen. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: The public glyph table (`modules/events/ui/glyphs.ts`) and the backoffice's (`shared/ui/status-glyphs.ts`) share no name, no public file imports `StatusChip`, and every name of either table is drawn by a file of its own surface (2026-10-11, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).
